q: Can a Japanese steel or aluminium exporter deduct GX emissions trading costs from CBAM?
title: Japan GX trading and the CBAM deduction
short: Only for a price effectively paid. Japan's GX emissions trading becomes mandatory for large emitters from 2026, with allowances largely free at first. Until a plant pays for allowances beyond its allocation, there is little to deduct. Keep the evidence ready.
audience: Japanese exporters of CBAM goods and their EU importers

p: Japan has moved its GX emissions trading from voluntary participation to a mandatory scheme for companies above an emissions threshold. Allocation is expected to be largely free in the early years.

ul: Allowances actually bought and surrendered beyond the free amount.
Any separate carbon levy actually paid.

p: The Commission decides how foreign carbon prices are recognised. Confirm the current rules and keep the allocation and surrender records for the year.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel, electricity and production documents into dated, fingerprinted installation records, the starting point for the actual emissions an EU importer asks for.
